note: Trailer-craft knowledge base for game-launch-strategist (references/08-trailer.md, trailer_kit.py). Every rule is PARAPHRASED from the source, never copied. 'date' = day the source was consulted; 'published' = the source's own date when known. strength: platform_doc = the platform's own documentation; measured = numbers from data or many cases; expert_opinion = a recognised practitioner; third_party = blog/tool guides, not official; internal = the owner's own decisions or notes for this project (only when the trailer kit is applied to that project). Re-verify platform specs before every render: they change.

rules.rule: Real gameplay on screen within the first 5 seconds; no studio, engine or publisher logos before it, no slow environment pans with 'in a world...' text.
rules.rule_it: Gioco vero entro 5 secondi; niente loghi di studio o motore all'inizio, niente panoramiche lente con frasi a effetto.

sources.what: How To Market A Game (Chris Zukowski): trailer rules for the Coming Soon page
GameDiscoverCo: the slow-burn trailer mistake, viewers skip ahead and leave
Derek Lieu: the 'thumbstopper' opening, no logos or slow establishing shots

rules.rule: The first shot changes (cut or decisive action beat) by about 3 s. Measured twice: 24 comparables on 2026-10-07 (best third median 2.9 s vs rest 6.9 s) and 14 genre trailers measured in full on 2026-10-21 (7 most-reviewed: median first cut 2.4 s, average shot 1.9 s; the other 7: 7.7 s and 3.4 s). Correlation, not proof: budget and genre confound it.
rules.rule_it: Il primo taglio (o un colpo di scena chiaro) arriva entro circa 3 secondi: i giochi che vendono di più tagliano prima.

sources.what: store_bench.py on 24 comparables (correlation weak, rho 0.17: an indication, not a law)
trailer_kit.py measure on 14 Steam trailers (full-length cuts, loudness, tempo)

rules.rule: Open with footage from deep into a session (hours, not minutes): the busiest, most developed state of the game, so viewers instantly recognise 'one of those games'.
rules.rule_it: Apri con il gioco 'avanzato' (sala piena, torre alta), non con i primi minuti: chi guarda deve capire subito che tipo di gioco è.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: first shot from hours into the game
Derek Lieu: 'gameplay grab bag' opening shows the mid/late game

rules.rule: A strong opening can be one uncut take of the basic loop with a three-act shape: set-up, conflict, consequence (often a comic failure). It feels raw and honest; a random chunk of play without the loop is weak.
rules.rule_it: Un'apertura forte può essere una sola ripresa senza tagli con inizio, problema e conseguenza (spesso un disastro comico).

sources.what: Derek Lieu: four ways to open, the Spelunky 'oner'

rules.rule: Establish the bedrock (what kind of game, what the player does) in the first 5-10 s before cutting faster; secondary features (cosmetics, modes, extras) come later because they multiply the core, they are not the core.
rules.rule_it: Prima si capisce cosa si fa nel gioco, poi si accelera; gli extra (costumi, modalità) vengono dopo.

sources.what: Derek Lieu, Sheepherds trailer makeover: first shot goes straight into the core action

rules.rule: Treat the trailer as a tutorial: one readable idea per shot, verbs and their results, then escalate from context to simple ideas to depth and finally scope.
rules.rule_it: Il trailer insegna il gioco: un'idea per inquadratura, cosa fai e cosa succede, poi sempre più difficile e ricco.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: game trailers as tutorials

rules.rule: Shape for a store trailer: thumbstopper (~1-10 s, a few clips of the loop and its depth), intro of the core verbs (~10-15 s), escalation (~40 s), climax of breadth and scope (~20-30 s), then title and call to action. Scale the parts down for 45-60 s.
rules.rule_it: Forma tipo: aggancio, cosa si fa, crescita, momento più forte, titolo e invito all'azione.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: 90 s structure and 30 s cutdown

rules.rule: Keep a store trailer under ~90 s unless very skilled; a 30-60 s gameplay trailer is enough for most indies (HTMAG: can be ~30 s). Comparables: median 79.8 s, best third 78.2 s, Balatro 38.6 s, PEAK 57 s, How to Fish 59 s.
rules.rule_it: Sotto i 90 secondi; per un indie bastano 45-60 secondi di gioco vero.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: under ~90 s
HTMAG: a trailer can be about 30 s
store_bench.py, 24 comparables

rules.rule: Move on before the viewer thinks 'I get it, what else?'; vary shot and section lengths; when a kind of content repeats, cut between varied examples quickly.
rules.rule_it: Cambia inquadratura prima che chi guarda si annoi; durate varie; se mostri cose simili, tagli più veloci.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: pacing

rules.rule: Group similar images in threes at most; make the third different or a transition into the next section.
rules.rule_it: Al massimo tre immagini simili di fila; la terza diversa o che porta alla parte dopo.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: montages in threes

rules.rule: After the climax give a slower beat so the audience can breathe; an earned quiet moment can linger. Mix close shots for impact with wide shots for context.
rules.rule_it: Dopo il momento più forte, una pausa che fa respirare; alterna primi piani e campi larghi.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: climax and release

rules.rule: Pick music with a dramatic arc and variety; sync key visual moments to it and let its build and release carry the climax. Bridge sections with a match cut, a carried movement or a sound cue.
rules.rule_it: Musica con un crescendo; i momenti chiave cadono sul ritmo; le parti si legano con un movimento o un suono.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: music and transitions

rules.rule: Valve recommends that the first trailer on the store page is primarily gameplay, often with the in-game HUD visible; the first two valid trailers show before the screenshots.
rules.rule_it: Steam consiglia che il primo trailer della pagina sia soprattutto gioco, spesso con l'interfaccia visibile; i primi due trailer vengono prima degli screenshot.

sources.what: Steamworks documentation: Trailers

rules.rule: Viewers may watch without any audio (Steam's own warning; third-party guides say the first store trailer autoplays muted): every beat must read with the sound off, text carries the meaning, audio only adds.
rules.rule_it: Molti guardano senza audio: il trailer deve capirsi a volume zero; il suono aggiunge, non spiega.

sources.what: Steamworks: customers may be watching without audio
presskit.gg: first trailer autoplays muted (third-party, [DA VERIFICARE] on the live store)

rules.rule: Steam builds a 6-second looping microtrailer from six 1-second segments of the first visible trailer and it cannot be customised: avoid long cards, black frames and static UI anywhere, because any second may be picked.
rules.rule_it: Steam crea da solo un mini-trailer di 6 secondi prendendo 6 pezzi da 1 secondo: ogni secondo del trailer deve essere bello e chiaro (niente nero, niente schermate ferme lunghe).

sources.what: Steamworks: microtrailers

rules.rule: In the Discovery Queue shoppers may give a game less than 10 s: the first 5-10 s alone must sell genre, tone and the unique verb.
rules.rule_it: Nella coda di scoperta di Steam si decide in meno di 10 secondi.

sources.what: Steamworks: Discovery Queue note

rules.rule: Upload the highest resolution up to 1920x1080, 30 or 60 fps, 5,000+ kbps, H.264 video + AAC audio in .mp4/.mov, 16:9 preferred, 44.1 or 48 kHz audio; a custom thumbnail must be a 1920x1080 frame of the video itself without text.
rules.rule_it: File per Steam: 1920x1080, 60 fps, almeno 5.000 kbps, H.264 + AAC, mp4; miniatura presa dal video, senza testo.

sources.what: Steamworks: trailer specs and thumbnails

rules.rule: Valve's review asks to remove trailers that show incomplete content or content planned for later: only show what is in the build the page promises (for a demo/beta page: what the demo contains, or label it).
rules.rule_it: Steam fa togliere i trailer che mostrano cose non ancora nel gioco: si mostra solo ciò che c'è.

sources.what: Steamworks: Review Process (read via search summary, [DA VERIFICARE] exact wording)

rules.rule: Everything in-engine and representative; a moment may be staged in the engine for the camera, but never a fake CG trailer. Shoppers check that it is not an asset flip: a real trailer is proof of care.
rules.rule_it: Tutto girato nel gioco vero; si può preparare una scena per la ripresa, mai un video finto.

sources.what: HTMAG: in-engine, no fake CG; asset flippers don't make trailers

rules.rule: Make the first trailer gameplay-focused and useful for both PR and the store; don't pile up trailers on the page without removing old ones.
rules.rule_it: Un trailer di gioco forte, usato sia per la stampa sia per la pagina; non accumulare trailer vecchi.

sources.what: GameDiscoverCo

rules.rule: Make a ~30 s cutdown with one or two full loops of the key verbs, upload natively on each platform (autoplay on phones), add a one-line pitch in the post and a link to the store page; add .srt captions where dialogue exists.
rules.rule_it: Versione da 30 secondi con uno o due giri completi del gioco, caricata direttamente su ogni social, con una frase che dice cos'è e il link Steam.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: social media optimisation

rules.rule: On TikTok/Shorts/Reels the hook must land in about 1-3 s; short and loopable (studio clips with many views average ~27-28 s).
rules.rule_it: Sui social verticali l'aggancio è nel primo secondo o due; video corti che si ripetono bene.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: 1-3 s on TikTok
skill evidence base (HTMAG, GameDiscoverCo, TikTok Creator Academy)
Jared Tan study via GameDiscoverCo: 27-28 s averages

rules.rule: On a 1080x1920 frame keep text and key action out of the platform UI: about 130 px top, 484 px bottom, 44 px left, 140 px right (most-quoted values; not official TikTok numbers, longer captions eat more of the bottom).
rules.rule_it: Nei video verticali niente testo vicino ai bordi: lascia libero in alto, molto in basso (didascalia) e a destra (pulsanti).

sources.what: Cadenus: TikTok safe zone template in pixels
Vertical safe zones TikTok/Reels/Shorts

rules.rule: One 1080x1920 9:16 H.264/AAC master serves TikTok, YouTube Shorts (Short if up to 180 s) and Reels (recommended to new audiences only up to 3 min; feed crops to 4:5, so keep key content in the centre).
rules.rule_it: Un solo file verticale 1080x1920 va bene per TikTok, Shorts e Reels; il centro dell'immagine deve contenere l'azione.

sources.what: Social media video length limits 2026
Reels length and recommendation limit

rules.rule: Master to about -14 LUFS integrated with true peak at or below -1 dBTP: YouTube-style players turn louder files down (never up), so louder only loses dynamics. It is a practical reference, not an official upload spec. Genre trailers measured 2026-10-21 range from -10.8 to -21.1 LUFS (median of the 7 most-reviewed -13.5).
rules.rule_it: Volume finale circa -14 LUFS con picchi sotto -1 dBTP: più forte non serve, le piattaforme abbassano.

sources.what: APU Software: -14 LUFS is a reference, not an official YouTube spec
EBU R128: -1 dBTP peak ceiling
trailer_kit.py measure, 14 Steam trailers

rules.rule: Text cards and captions must be readable on a phone: short (3-6 words), on screen at least ~0.3 s per word fully settled, cap height at least ~4% of frame height (wide) / ~3% (vertical, 1920 px), strong contrast; one text element at a time.
rules.rule_it: Scritte corte e grandi, leggibili sul telefono, ferme abbastanza da leggerle, una alla volta.

sources.what: Buffet Panic! v1 trailer study: 0.3 s/word hold that the owner judged readable (internal practice)
Derek Lieu: viewers read a one-line pitch faster than they watch

rules.rule: No static menu or UI screen held for more than ~1 s without something moving or being chosen: menus are shown as an action (a click, a card flipping, a number changing), never as a still.
rules.rule_it: Mai un menu fermo per più di un secondo: si mostra solo mentre succede qualcosa (un clic, un numero che cambia).

sources.what: Derek Lieu: show interactions and their results
Steamworks microtrailer sampling (any second can be picked)

rules.rule: End on the title and one clear call to action that matches the date (before the store page: follow; with the page: 'Wishlist on Steam'; with a demo: 'Play the free demo'); hold the end card 3-4 s, no more.
rules.rule_it: Finale: titolo e un solo invito chiaro adatto al momento (Wishlist su Steam, demo gratis), tenuto 3-4 secondi.

sources.what: Derek Lieu: teaser ends with title and call to action
simulated panel on trailer v2: end card too long (SIMULATO, ranks issues only)

rules.rule: Store-page GIFs/looping videos: 3-8 s of one verb and its result, seamless loop (last frame flows into the first), no text needed, under the platform size limit; the best comparables use more looping videos in the description (median 7.5 vs 3.5).
rules.rule_it: Le GIF della pagina: 3-8 secondi di una sola azione con il suo risultato, che si ripete senza scatti.

sources.what: store_bench.py: looping_videos median best third 7.5 vs rest 3.5 (rho 0.34, moderate)

rules.rule: Steam's content survey asks developers to disclose pre-generated AI content that appears in the game OR in marketing material and the store page (efficiency tools such as code assistants are exempt; update reported 2026-01-16). Whether code-written procedural audio/images count is not stated: check the live Steamworks page and let the owner decide.
rules.rule_it: Steam chiede di dichiarare i contenuti generati con l'AI anche nel marketing (trailer, pagina). Se musica o immagini fatte con codice contino non è scritto: va controllato sulla pagina ufficiale e deciso dal proprietario.

sources.what: Game Developer: Valve clarifies AI disclosure rules ([DA VERIFICARE] on the current Steamworks page)

rules.rule: Use only CC0, CC-BY (with credit in the description/credits ledger) or licences that explicitly allow commercial video use; never CC-BY-NC, 'personal use', unknown or Content-ID-registered tracks; log every file in a credits ledger with URL, licence and date.
rules.rule_it: Solo musica, suoni e immagini con licenza pulita (CC0 o CC-BY con credito), mai 'non commerciale'; ogni file nel registro dei crediti.

sources.what: Freesound FAQ: CC0, BY, BY-NC (no commercial use)
Pixabay Content License: free, no attribution, no standalone redistribution

steam.microtrailer: 6 x 1 s from first trailer, not customisable
steam.thumbnail: 1920x1080 frame from the video, no text

negative_base: studio, engine or publisher logos before the first gameplay frame
slow establishing pan of an empty environment with 'in a world...' text
random or automatic zooms, Ken Burns pushes, punch-ins that the edit did not motivate
shaky handheld fake camera, dutch angles without reason
any menu, shop or UI screen held still for more than 1 second
black frames, fades to black inside the first 10 seconds
cuts in the middle of an action before it resolves
the same gag or sticker repeated more than twice
two text elements on screen at the same time
text that relies on sound to make sense; dialogue-only beats
voice-over or narration
footage of features not in the build the page promises
pre-rendered CG or mock-up footage presented as gameplay
clipping or interpenetration of characters and props, characters cut by the frame edge in a way that hides their head
UI prompts, debug overlays, FPS counters, editor gizmos, cursor of the OS
watermarks, stock-footage looks, generic 'epic' trailer music, risers with no payoff
audio louder than -13 LUFS integrated or peaks above -1 dBTP
personal names, team names or credits other than the official credit line
any mention of AI, generative tools or how the trailer was made
fake review quotes, awards or press logos that do not exist
a URL typed in the video
end card longer than 4 seconds
